Dynamic Graph Neural Networks have been highlighted as a core approach for modeling evolving user preferences in sequential recommendation [S2:286d2e0f3d882a37f486623c716d8a54a4a58fdc]. Graph‑Based Embedding Smoothing is presented as a technique to capture dynamic and evolutionary preferences through behavior sequences [S2:b9915d00a7f46e51e587aff4365e1c48ab8ef496]. A Comparative Analysis of Heterogeneous and Homogeneous GraphSAGE models demonstrates their applicability to movie recommendation tasks [S2:13109adf6edd2d222605ec5cd1d12fe6c18f2fff].

Factorizing personalized Markov chains (FPMC) introduced a tensor factorization framework that integrates matrix factorization with Markov chain dynamics for next‑basket recommendation [S2:50d85cb114f7c5e779a6772f2931e77dddd54a5e]. Fusing Similarity Models with Markov Chains (FOSSIL) extended this line by combining item similarity with factorized Markov chains to address sparsity in sequential recommendation [S2:fea7e2bcbe852bcb33ce70a4d57664e954f0e82a]. S‑Walk advanced session‑based recommendation by employing random walks to capture intra‑session transitions while scaling to large datasets [S2:2be2e23c1ba6c2c62a85ac2ab7968d5e657ed8c6]. Continuous‑Time Sequential Recommendation with Temporal Graph Collaborative Transformer reported superior performance over FPMC by learning time‑aware embeddings from ordered purchase sequences [S2:3418602757a13aa3abcb850d6ffba9ff930b3784].
